title: Anchored Priming Signal Calibration Manifest
author: Elena Morales
content:
Overview

This document defines the Anchored Priming Signal Calibration Manifest: a reproducible, low-overhead procedure and artifact schema for generating, calibrating, and validating priming probes that target signal stability across quantized and KV-cache-enabled inference platforms. The goal is to provide a cross-workload reference that ties priming templates to measurable telemetry, acceptance thresholds, and remediation routes so model onboarding, shadow rollouts and regression triage teams can objectively decide whether a priming variant is safe to promote.

Why this exists

- Priming (system messages, few-shot exemplars, and structured context) is a major source of variability when models change or when quantization/latency optimizations are applied.
- Current onboarding checks focus on bulk quality metrics; we need a focused calibration surface that isolates priming-induced deltas and links them to telemetry.
- This manifest standardizes probe construction, calibration steps, and an artifact format that the eval harness and runtime can consume.

Scope and non-goals

- In-scope: generation and calibration of priming probes for text and multi-turn prompt families; metrics and thresholds for quantitative gating; artifact schema for probe packaging; remediation guidance for quant and cache-sensitive failures.
- Out-of-scope: annotator training materials (see prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/annotator-calibration), full model retraining, and downstream product UX changes.

Definitions

- Anchored priming probe: a prompt instance constructed from a stable anchor (canonical instruction, control exemplars, or a short seed context) plus a small set of perturbations used to measure sensitivity.
- Calibration run: a defined execution of a probe across an ensemble of model variants and runtime configurations (e.g., fp16 vs int8, fresh vs warm KV cache).
- Stability delta: a numeric measure describing difference in semantic outputs computed by similarity metrics or task-specific scores (see Metrics section).

Artifact format (single-file manifest)

- File: priming-manifest.toml (example fields described below)

Required fields (table):

| Field | Type | Description | Example |
|---|---|---:|---|
| manifest_id | string | stable id for the probe manifest | anch-priming-v1 |
| anchor_source | string | canonical instruction or dataset id | instruction-registry/clarify-order |
| perturbation_family | string | short descriptor for perturbation style | paraphrase, punctuation-noise |
| target_tasks | string | comma-separated task identifiers | summarization, intent-class |
| seeds | string | comma-separated seed ids used to derive probes | s001,s002 |
| generation_params | string | short JSON blob (escaped) with gen knobs | {"temperature":0.2,"max_tokens":200} |
| eval_matrix | string | path/id to eval slice matrix used | eval-sets/anchored-priming/2025-03 |
| owner | string | document owner team/person | priya-ml |

Probe generation guidelines

1. Anchor selection: pick a short canonical instruction or system message that represents the family (<= 140 characters).
2. Deterministic seeds: derive 8–16 seeds via the seeded paraphrase generator in the evaluator SDK to cover syntactic variation without changing intent.
3. Perturbation budget: for each seed, create up to four perturbations: (a) whitespace/punctuation noise, (b) synthetic entity anonymization, (c) few-shot exemplar swap, (d) constraint augmentation (add or remove a constraint).
4. Packaging: assemble probes into the manifest with metadata, expected gold labels (if applicable), and a candidate acceptance-policy block (see Policy section).

Calibration run procedure (operational steps)

1. Prepare runtime matrix: select model variants and runtime configs to test. Minimum matrix: baseline float32 model (dev), target quantized variant (int8), and warm vs cold KV cache states.
2. Bake manifest into eval harness: register manifest with id in the evaluator service and tag runs with artifact manifest_id.
3. Execute three passes:
   a. Warmup pass: 250 synthetic probes to establish baseline latency and token distribution.
   b. Anchored calibration: run all anchors x seeds x perturbations across matrix.
   c. Noise sweep: run additional stochastic perturbations (temperature or sampling seeds) to measure variance.
4. Collect telemetry: store outputs, per-token latency, attention-kv-hits, tokenization divergences, and model logprobs.
5. Compute stability deltas and quality deltas across matrix and compare to thresholds.

Metrics and thresholds (recommended)

- Semantic Similarity (SSIM): embed-based cosine similarity between baseline and variant response; gate failure if median < 0.88.
- Task Score Delta: for closed tasks (e.g., classification) require delta <= 2% absolute drop.
- Response Length Delta: warn if median change > 20% unless intentional.
- Tokenization Drift: fraction of probes where token count differs by >15% flagged.
- KV Cache Sensitivity: percentage of probes with >5% change in latency when moving from warm to cold cache triggers deeper triage.

Example thresholds table:

| Metric | Accept | Caution | Reject | Action |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Median cosine similarity to baseline | >= 0.90 | 0.88–0.90 | < 0.88 | Fail quant rollout, open regression ticket |
| Median task score delta | <= 1% | 1–2% | > 2% | Pause promotion, run human annotation |
| KV-sensitivity (latency increase) | <= 5% | 5–15% | > 15% | Evaluate cache fallback policy |

Automated gating and human escalation policy

- Automated gates in the eval harness will mark a manifest run as PASS / WARN / FAIL according to thresholds above.
- On WARN: notify model-onboarding and runtime-ops channels; require a short-form human review within 48 hours.
- On FAIL: automatic block on promotion; create a regression-triage issue with attached artifacts and owner assignment.

Runbook: triage sequence for a FAIL

1. Reproduce: re-run the manifest on the same matrix to rule out transient noise. Document differences.
2. Narrow: run a minimal subset (single anchor, single seed) to find which perturbation causes divergence.
3. Isolate: test with and without quantization and with cold/warm cache to attribute to runtime or model weights.
4. Hypothesize and patch: possible mitigations: prompt rewrite to reduce fragile constructs, alternate exemplar selection, quantization-profile adjustment, or KV-cache pre-warming policy.
5. Validate: after mitigation, run the anchored manifest to confirm stability metrics recover.

Suggested remediation patterns (short descriptions)

- Prompt canonicalization: replace fragile wording with deterministic phrases; prefer constrained templates for critical tasks.
- Greedy exemplar selection: choose exemplars that minimize ambiguity across seeds (scored by semantic overlap).
- Quant-hedge profile: fallback to a higher-precision execution on specific slices (defined by manifest labels) when gate conditions trigger.
- Cache-shim: insert a synthetic warmup call with a short prefix to prime KV cache for known-sensitive anchors.

Artifact consumption by downstream systems

- Evaluator: consumes the manifest to schedule calibration runs and expose PASS/WARN/FAIL status to the model-onboard workflow.
- Runtime: can read the manifest labels to apply quant-hedge or cache-shim policies at routing time.
- Monitor: attaches run ids to telemetry dashboards (per-manifest breakdown) and correlates with production probe traffic via the probe id.

Operational ownership and lifecycle

- Owner: Applied ML steward (see owner field in manifest).
- Review cadence: re-calibrate manifests quarterly or on model version changes.
- Retirement: manifests not executed for 12 months must be archived and revalidated before reuse.

Example CLI snippets

- Register manifest: evaluatorctl register --file priming-manifest.toml --team priya-ml --env staging
- Run calibration: evaluatorctl run --manifest anch-priming-v1 --matrix matrix/quant-warm-cold --tag anchored-cal-2025-07
- Fetch results: evaluatorctl results --run anchored-cal-2025-07 --format json > anchored-cal-2025-07-results.json

Examples (short)

- Summarization anchor: "Summarize the following chat for a billing-focused support agent." Seeds: paraphrases preserving 'billing' focus. Perturbations: redact amounts, reorder turns, shorten context. Expectation: high semantic overlap and stable extraction of billing items.

- Intent classification anchor: single-sentence instruction with a one-shot exemplar. Perturbations: entity name swap and punctuation noise. Expectation: <1% task score delta across quantized vs baseline.

Reporting and dashboards

- Dashboards must present: per-manifest stability heatmap (models x perturbations), run-level PASS/WARN/FAIL, distribution of similarity scores, and KV cache sensitivity summary.
- Alerting: FAIL state should create a JIRA regression issue via automation and page the model-onboard rotation on-call if the manifest is tagged 'critical'.

Appendix: example priming-manifest.toml (simplified)

manifest_id = "anch-priming-v1"
anchor_source = "instruction-registry/clarify-order"
perturbation_family = "paraphrase-punct"
target_tasks = "summarization,slot-extract"
seeds = "s001,s002,s003"
generation_params = '{"temperature":0.0,"top_p":0.9,"max_tokens":120}'
eval_matrix = "matrix/standard-quant-warmcold"
owner = "elena-morales"
